- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment phases (sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot, especially after spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment phases (sentiment < 0.3) — model is too conservative, often missing upward momentum.
- Lagged corrections: model often fails to adjust early in a trend; true price moves faster than forecasted, especially in high-sentiment periods.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimating sustained trends.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early stages of upward momentum; later in the cycle, model underestimates peak prices.
- Spike recovery: after sharp price spikes, model underestimates the rebound, leading to premature downward corrections.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment is rising, add 2–3% to forecast; if falling, subtract 1–2% to account for volatility suppression.
